skills.trigger: When evaluating a focal hyperdense opacity within the airways on CT to determine its composition and etiology.
steps: Place a Region of Interest (ROI) measurement tool directly over the hyperdense object within the bronchus.

Compare the measured Hounsfield Unit (HU) value against standard tissue densities: metallic foreign bodies typically exhibit very high attenuation (>400 HU), whereas mucous plugs, blood, or soft tissue masses generally range between 20-80 HU.
Distinguish foreign body obstruction from mucous plugging by confirming the presence of metallic-density attenuation rather than soft-tissue density.

skills.trigger: When interpreting distal lung parenchymal changes associated with a central airway abnormality to determine the underlying pathophysiology.
steps: Identify the specific pattern of distal lung change: look for volume loss (atelectasis) versus volume expansion (hyperinflation/air trapping).

Correlate the direction of volume change with the type of obstruction: complete obstruction typically leads to resorptive atelectasis (volume loss), while ball-valve partial obstruction leads to air trapping (hyperinflation).

Differentiate progressive atelectasis caused by foreign body aspiration from other causes like pneumonia (which presents as consolidation without significant volume loss initially) or interstitial disease (diffuse pattern) by linking the focal airway blockage to the specific lobar collapse.
